lessons.definition: Additionality means payments fund new conservation that would not have happened otherwise, while leakage is the unintended displacement of environmental harm.
lessons.plain: Additionality checks if a green project actually creates extra benefits instead of paying for things that were already going to happen. Leakage happens when protecting one area just pushes harmful building or farming into a different neighborhood or nearby hillsides.
lessons.example: If Kabul pays to protect a hillside park, but developers simply clear a nearby peri-urban agricultural field instead, that is leakage.
lessons.connects: It connects to governance, effectiveness of green infrastructure, and how we measure real ecological benefits versus on-paper plans.
lessons.why_phd: Essential for your thesis to prove your proposed environmental planning interventions actually change outcomes instead of just shifting problems elsewhere.

quiz.q: What does additionality mean in payments for ecosystem services?
quiz.a: It means the conservation benefits would not have occurred without the payment program.

quiz.q: How is leakage defined in this context?
quiz.a: It is the unintended shifting of environmental harm or land-use change to another location.
